generatedBy: the V02 packaging step (vendor-pocket-tts), which vendors every asset below from its pinned revision and refuses to write an artifact whose bytes do not hash to the recorded value

notes: This manifest travels with the pack, so by itself it proves nothing: a substituted pack can carry a rewritten, self-consistent manifest. This block is what makes the release signed instead — it declares that install.mjs must refuse to stage a pack without a valid Developer ID signature record, and the trust anchor (identity, team and pinned public key) lives in scripts/release/installers.json distribution, never in the pack.

The signature record covers the exact bytes of this manifest and the sha256 of the whole pack directory, so an added, removed or edited file anywhere in the pack invalidates it even when the manifest was rewritten to match. A store that has committed a signed version keeps requiring a signature (policy.json), so an update cannot drop back to unsigned.

notes: Payloads are vendored by the packaging step (vendor-pocket-tts) and are not checked into this repository; every sha256/bytes pair is the artifact record that step enforces and refuses to deviate from, and scripts/release/verify-pack.mjs re-verifies every pin against a pack before install.

The asr (Whisper small.en), reasoner (Qwen3.5-4B q4) and runtime (bundled CPython) entries complete the offline A+B asset set the Q03 installer embeds. Their digests/lengths are the vendor-step artifact records for the pinned revisions; a checkout that does not hold the vendored payloads cannot recompute them, exactly as for the Pocket TTS weights and voices above. The runtime pin matches python.archiveSha256 in workers/pocket-tts/runtime.json.
offlineInstall declares the whole-journey contract: the full installer needs no account or API key and performs no run-time downloads; every asset above is resolved from the installed bundle.
